authoring: Extracted by SportFisherGameplay (Art/_sportFisherGameplay.js) from the rig source at the hash above — the rig itself is unedited. Polygons are computed by the rig’s own station/hbOf/dfrac/sheerZ/bowRake and the house volumes’ own plan functions; fit-out footprints are transcribed hull-spec literals with per-item provenance. _excluded.WASHBOARD: NO washboards on this hull, and this is the load-bearing absence. The rig draws a deck margin alongside the house, but measured at the deck line it is 0.071–0.612 m wide (11 samples, y -9.65 → 1.53, widening only as the house nose narrows into the foredeck): a reveal between the house side and the covering board, not a strip anyone walks. It is that narrow by design — clampHW lands the house sides on the cap so the covering board reads as ONE unbroken line stem to transom. Consequence: cockpit and foredeck are separate walkable islands on the exterior.
_excluded.covering_board: The teak cap outboard of the reveal is rolled and carries a toe rail lifting to 0.2 m forward of u=0.55 — a boundary, not a surface.
_excluded.house_interior: Salon and skylounge are modelled as an exterior volume only — no interior floor exists to walk.
_excluded.bridge_access_interior: The only modelled exterior climb is aft deck → helm coaming (LADDER.bridge_ladder); salon→skylounge is the interior companionway (STAIRS.house_to_bridge).
_excluded.foredeck_access: Nothing in the rig connects the cockpit to the foredeck: no margin wide enough to walk, no ladder, no door in the house exterior other than the aft glass. Any walk-forward move a character makes on this hull has to be authored game-side.
_excluded.gear_above: Outriggers, tower pipework, whips, radomes, hardtop slab and rod tubes are gear over the decks, not surfaces. Rod points are ANCHORS.rods.
_excluded.topside_detail: Hull windows, louvre vents and the boot/cove bands are paint and detail, outside any walkable surface.
_excluded.skylounge: the skylounge (L2) is dressed — one companionway carries salon→bridge whole (flagged in STAIRS); its helm is not an interior interactable this pass
_excluded.foredeck_route: no exterior route cockpit→foredeck — the extractor finding stands
_excluded.below_aft: the below flat’s aft end tucks under the raised salon — full headroom holds only forward of the trunk (authored abstraction, flagged)
_excluded.engine_room: machinery space aft of the flat under the salon (y < 0.20) — dressed; access via the cockpit hatches (extractor sole_hatches)
_excluded.rode_locker: forepeak rode + thruster space forward of y 6.80 — dressed
_excluded.crew_cabin: crew cabin abaft the engine room stays OUT with the machinery space — prize-boat guest spaces only this pass

_confirm.cleat_identification: All three CLEATS entries are read from unlabelled iron fittings (see each provenance). Positions are exact; the reading as tie-offs is the art side’s, and a gameplay ruling can demote any of them.
_confirm.upper_decks: bridge_sole, helm_coaming, aft_deck are included because they are real modelled surfaces with real dimensions. If gameplay only ever walks the cockpit, mezzanine, side decks and foredeck, the upper polygons are inert data — they are not a claim that a character can reach them.

_supersedes_convention: LF/blob sha256 of the file this replaces, as stored in git. The working tree is CRLF on Windows (autocrlf), whose digest is c246b2058def025ee26c91e083c7a5346e574d9899b0e23eab366311335c6936 — the same file, the other convention. Answer in LF.

_corrections_on_intake.why: This file was adopted from the 2026-08-28 changeset with three corrections. It is NOT byte-identical to what was sent; re-running the extractor without reading this key will reintroduce all three.
_corrections_on_intake._supersedes: The drop declared _supersedes 20aa9bc7cc43090ff3589adece79335aa5f15f3552abcd118230fe221eec1e17 — the sha of UPSTREAM'S OWN 2026-08-27 export, the one #678 refused as internally inconsistent (it deleted the 9.74 coaming while leaving bridge_ladder climbing to 9.55). That file was never in this repository, so the field named a predecessor we never held. Re-stamped to the digest of the file actually replaced.
_corrections_on_intake.helm_coaming.polygon: The drop's 42 vertices differ from the rig's own ring on 38 of 42, by up to 0.050 m in x (y is identical — the same stations). Reproduced exactly, all 42 vertices to zero error, by interpolating the volume's `hw` half-breadth table LINEARLY; the rig interpolates it through mono(), a Fritsch–Carlson monotone cubic. The deviation is zero at the four hw knots (y -1.1, -2.5, -4.5, -8.75) and peaks mid-segment, which is the signature. Restored to the ring the rig itself emits: (±(P(t,z1).x − 0.16), P(t,z1).y) over t=0..1 in TS order, run in ClearScript V8 against hull-rigs/sportFisherIsoRig2.js (205a93c9…) — and identical against docs/art/rigs/sportFisherIsoRig2.js (152eb5f3…), so the root/kit rig split is not the cause. This is the ONE number in the file the drop changed that was already right.
_corrections_on_intake.helm_coaming._notes.helm_seats: New note, kept — but its footprint (±0.25) and top (0.75 m) matched neither the rig nor each other, and the _confirm flag covered only the halfwidth. Replaced with the box measured out of the rig's face stream: ±0.28 / ±0.24, top 0.60 m. The value the drop replaced already carried 0.60 correctly, in prose, inside helm_pod's note.
_corrections_on_intake.accepted_unchanged: The id split itself (bridge_sole = the 7.30 skylounge, new helm_coaming = the 9.74 coaming), LADDER.bridge_ladder → [aft_deck, helm_coaming], STAIRS.house_to_bridge.opening.in → bridge_sole, derivedFromRigSha256 → 205a93c9…, helm_pod.height_above_floor_m.top 0.78 → 0.83, and every reworded note.
